options: The practice of backing up databases on a schedule
The practice of structuring, describing and organising information so it reflects real-world entities, relationships, rules and contexts
The practice of writing SQL queries for reports
The practice of tuning database indexes for speed
The practice of migrating data between cloud providers
questions.explanation: Data Modelling structures, describes and organises information to reflect real-world entities, relationships, rules and contexts in support of operations, analytics, governance and AI.

questions.stem: Approximately how many Data Modelling techniques exist, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
questions.explanation: Most people know only a few techniques, but in reality there are around 37 of them.

questions.stem: Storing all of an employee's details (ID, name, mobile, address, salary, department) in one row of a spreadsheet illustrates which kind of data model?
questions.explanation: Keeping all information for one employee in a single row is the Denormalisation data model.

questions.stem: In the monthly salary example, which option represents data modelling in the Normalisation way?
options: Replacing the first month's salary with the second month's salary
Adding a new column such as salary_2ndmonth every month
Breaking employee details into separate Employee and Salary tables, carrying the employee ID into the Salary table
Storing salaries in a text file outside the database
questions.explanation: Splitting the data into an Employee table and a monthly Salary table, linked by employee ID, is Normalisation.

questions.stem: Why is adding a new salary column for every month not a viable option?
options: Because databases forbid more than one salary column
Because you would have to add a new column every month
Because salaries cannot be stored as numbers
Because it would delete the employee ID
Because it would violate a dimensional schema
questions.explanation: Adding a salary_2ndmonth style column means a new column must be added every month, which is not viable.

options: Two tables joined with each other
Three tables joined through an intermediate table
A column that depends on another column within the same table, giving an internal join
A fact table joined to a dimension table
questions.explanation: A Unary Relationship is where a column depends on another column within the same table, in other words an internal join.

questions.stem: Which relationship type involves three tables joined with the help of an intermediate table?
questions.explanation: A Ternary Relationship joins three tables with the help of another intermediate table.

questions.stem: Which data modelling scheme uses a fact table joined with dimension tables, as in Star and Snowflake schemas?
questions.explanation: Star and Snowflake schemas are examples of the Dimensional scheme, where a fact table joins with dimension tables.

questions.stem: Which scheme is described as a graphical language for modelling software itself, consisting of a Class Model with entity types and relationship types?
questions.explanation: Object-Oriented (UML) is a graphical language for modelling software, made up of a Class Model with entity types and relationship types.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the NoSQL database kinds named in the Data Modelling schemes?
questions.explanation: NoSQL databases are graph, document, key-value and column-oriented; a Star schema belongs to Dimensional modelling.
